openQuestions.q: CHK-003's own verificationIntent is internally inconsistent about agy's host_run usage receipt, and that inconsistency is not a hypothetical edge case -- agy NEVER reports an output token count. Happy-path CHK-003:happy:0 requires the document to cite 'a reported output token count' for BOTH the Claude and the agy host_run receipt. Adversarial-path CHK-003:adversarial:0 requires receipt capture to 'fail closed' / be 'refused' whenever either host's 'output token field is absent'. But docs/host-run-usage.md states agy is unconditionally recorded as source=unavailable with no token count ever ('agy print mode exposes no usage surface (verified 2026-07-10), so no counts can be reported') -- which is exactly what CHK-003's own edge-path intent (CHK-003:edge:0) says is legitimate, honestly-cited evidence, not a failure. As worded, the agy leg of CHK-003 can never satisfy 'happy' and will always trip the literal 'adversarial' fail-closed trigger, while the edge intent says that same state is fine. Which reading should the DEV-phase implementer and the delivery/test-coverage reviewers use: (a) treat agy's guaranteed source=unavailable receipt (recordId + host + explicit unavailableReason, no token count) as satisfying CHK-003's happy path for the agy leg, with the adversarial trigger reserved for a genuinely missing recordId/no-run-at-all, or (b) reword CHK-003's happy/adversarial verificationIntent before DEV so the achievable-per-host outcome (numeric count for claude, honest unavailable for agy) is what 'happy' actually means?
openQuestions.evidence: checklist.json CHK-003 happy[0].desc: 'the document cites two distinct host_run receipts (recordId with llmuse_ prefix, host, and reported output token count)...'; adversarial[0].desc: '...or its output token field is absent when CHK-003 evidence is recorded -> receipt capture fails closed...'; edge[0].desc: 'One host_run receipt reports usage as recorded=unavailable...even though the audit itself completed -> the document does not fabricate an output token count for that host; it cites the receipt's actual unavailable/reason state...'. docs/host-run-usage.md #Per-host usage semantics: 'agy -- recorded as source=unavailable with provider antigravity and an explicit unavailableReason. agy print mode exposes no usage surface (verified 2026-07-10), so no counts can be reported.'
